chunks.title: Ask Kumail (this project)
chunks.text: Ask Kumail is a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) assistant and a remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) server over Kumail's resume and project documentation. Built with Next.js, TypeScript and the Vercel AI SDK, deployed on Vercel.

chunks.title: Ask Kumail (this project)
chunks.text: Documents are split by markdown headings into chunks, and each chunk keeps its document title and section path as a header. Retrieval is hybrid: BM25 keyword scoring and embedding cosine similarity (OpenAI text-embedding-3-small through the Vercel AI Gateway) each produce a ranking, and the two rankings are merged with reciprocal rank fusion. The top chunks are sent to the model, which must answer only from them and cite them by number.

chunks.title: Ask Kumail (this project)
chunks.text: The /api/mcp endpoint is a stateless Streamable HTTP MCP server with three tools: search_docs, ask_kumail and list_projects. Any MCP client, such as Claude, can connect to it by URL.

chunks.title: Ask Kumail (this project)
chunks.text: A labeled question set measures whether the correct document appears in the top results (hit@1, hit@3, MRR) for keyword-only, vector-only and hybrid retrieval.

chunks.title: Fade Kings booking app
chunks.text:
A full-stack Next.js booking app (demo build) for Fade Kings Barber Shop (Lynnwood): customers can browse the crew and prices without an account, book a chair as a guest or a member, track appointments, and earn rewards; barbers approve/decline requests, manage weekly availability and services, and post work photos/videos.

Stack: **Next.js 14 (App Router) + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS + Supabase** (Postgres, Auth, Storage).

chunks.title: Fade Kings booking app
chunks.section: Fade Kings Barber Shop — Lynnwood > 1. Create a Supabase project
chunks.text:
1. Go to [supabase.com](https://supabase.com) → New Project.
2. Once it's up, open **SQL Editor** → paste the contents of [`supabase/schema.sql`](./supabase/schema.sql) → Run. This creates every table, row-level-security policy, and the `posts` storage bucket used by the app.
3. Go to **Project Settings → API** and copy the **Project URL** and **anon public key**.
4. In **Authentication → Sign In / Providers**, turn on:
   - **Phone** (customers sign up/log in with phone + password — no SMS provider needed, see below)
   - **Anonymous sign-ins** (powers guest checkout)
5. In **Authentication → Settings**, turn on **"Auto confirm"** for both email and phone (or use the Management API to set `mailer_autoconfirm` / `sms_autoconfirm` to `true`). Without this, new accounts sit unconfirmed and can't write their profile row — the app has no email/SMS-sending step, so autoconfirm is required, not just a testing convenience.

chunks.title: Fade Kings booking app
chunks.section: Fade Kings Barber Shop — Lynnwood > 2. Configure the app
chunks.text:
```bash
cp .env.example .env.local
```

Fill in `.env.local`:

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://your-project.supabase.co
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=your-anon-key
```

chunks.title: Fade Kings booking app
chunks.section: Fade Kings Barber Shop — Lynnwood > 3. Run locally
chunks.text:
```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) — you'll land on `/auth`. Sign up once as a **Barber** (email + password, add at least one service) so there's someone to book. Customers don't need an account at all: click **"Browse Without Signing Up"** to look around and book — an account only gets created (as a phone-number login) if they choose to save the appointment afterward.

chunks.title: Fade Kings booking app
chunks.section: Fade Kings Barber Shop — Lynnwood > 4. Deploy
chunks.text:
The fastest path is **Vercel**:

1. Push this folder to a GitHub repo (see below).
2. Go to [vercel.com/new](https://vercel.com/new) → import the repo.
3. Add the two env vars from step 2 in the Vercel project settings.
4. Deploy. Vercel auto-detects Next.js — no build config needed.

Any other Node host (Railway, Render, Netlify, self-hosted) works too since this is a standard Next.js app — just set the same two env vars and run `npm run build && npm start`.

chunks.title: Fade Kings booking app
chunks.section: Fade Kings Barber Shop — Lynnwood > Pushing to GitHub
chunks.text:
No GitHub connection was active in this session, so the code lives in this folder rather than a repo. To publish it:

```bash
cd fade-kings   # this folder
git init
git add .
git commit -m "Fade Kings Barber Shop — initial build"
git branch -M main
git remote add origin https://github.com/<your-username>/<your-repo>.git
git push -u origin main
```

(Create the empty repo on GitHub first, or use `gh repo create` if you have the GitHub CLI.)

2. Promote your own account to owner. Sign up on the live site first (any role — Customer is simplest, just phone + password), then find your user's UUID in **Authentication → Users**, and run in SQL Editor:

chunks.title: Ops Automation
chunks.text: Ops-Automation is a scheduled-task automation dashboard — a set of small, real operations workflows that run on a schedule, log what they did, and present the results in a tabbed dashboard.

chunks.title: Ops Automation
chunks.text:
- **Job-board crawler** (`api/job-board-crawler.js`): fetches remote job postings from the Remotive API, filters them by role and keyword, de-duplicates them, and stores matches in Supabase — with a sample job included so the UI works before any API is configured.
- **CRM lead enrichment** (`api/crm-enrichment.js`): enriches leads with company domain, size, industry, and an engagement score, and records the enriched leads in Supabase.
- **Interview scheduler** (`api/interview-scheduler.js`): finds overlapping availability between a candidate and an interviewer (interval intersection), proposes time slots, and logs scheduled interviews.
- **Overdue follow-up drafting** (`api/overdue-followup.js`): finds overdue follow-ups and drafts follow-up messages for them.
- **Run logging and dashboard**: every workflow run is written to `workflow_runs` in Supabase, and the dashboard in `public/` shows Overview, Workflows, Activity, and Schedule tabs, with run history and per-workflow status.

chunks.title: PawPass
chunks.text: PawPass is a lightweight web platform designed for animal shelters and foster volunteers to easily transfer pet information between shifts, volunteers, fosters, and shelters without relying on emails and Excel sheets. The application is built as a Progressive Web App (PWA) with offline functionality and database persistence, featuring a custom logo and user-friendly interface that facilitates seamless pet care coordination.

chunks.title: PawPass
chunks.text:
- **Pet Profiles**: Create and manage detailed pet information
- **Care Updates**: Log updates about pet care and behavior
- **Shift Checklists**: Track completed care tasks during shifts
- **Image Upload**: Upload and manage pet photos
- **Emergency Flagging**: Mark pets requiring urgent care
- **Progressive Web App**: Works offline and can be installed on devices
- **Accessibility**: Color-blind friendly mode
- **Search Functionality**: Quickly find pets by name

chunks.title: PawPass
chunks.text: The application follows a modular architecture with the following components:

chunks.title: PawPass
chunks.text:

- **Email**: Email processing and notifications
- **AI**: AI integration for pet care recommendations
- **Encryption**: Data security and encryption

chunks.text:

- **Database**: PostgreSQL
- **ORM**: SQLAlchemy
- **Frontend**: HTML, CSS, JavaScript

chunks.title: Qmail
chunks.section: QMail - AI Scam Detection for Email
chunks.text:
QMail is a Progressive Web App (PWA) that flags scam and phishing emails with OpenAI, suggests actions, and helps clean up an inbox.

**Team project, WSU Hackathon 2025 (5th place).** Original repo: [garv-seth/qmail](https://github.com/garv-seth/qmail). This fork hosts the public demo: [qmail-demo-kumailr.vercel.app](https://qmail-demo-kumailr.vercel.app).

My role (Kumail Rizvi): branding, UX design, and project documentation.

chunks.title: Qmail
chunks.section: QMail - AI Scam Detection for Email > Features
chunks.text:
- AI email analysis: message text is sent to the OpenAI API with a structured JSON response, which returns a scam label, confidence, reasoning and a recommended action
- Encrypted storage: messages are encrypted with AES-256-GCM using random keys from Node's `crypto` module
- Smart filtering: categorizes emails and suggests actions
- Unsubscribe assistant: helps unsubscribe from unwanted newsletters
- Installable PWA with a mobile-friendly interface

chunks.title: Qmail
chunks.section: QMail - AI Scam Detection for Email > Tech Stack
chunks.text:
- Frontend: React with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui components
- Backend: Node.js with Express
- Database: PostgreSQL with Drizzle ORM
- Authentication: OpenID Connect (Replit Auth); the public demo uses a demo sign-in
- AI: OpenAI API for email analysis

chunks.title: Qmail
chunks.section: QMail - AI Scam Detection for Email > Notes
chunks.text: `server/azure-quantum.ts` contains an optional hook to source key randomness from an external random-number service. It is disabled in the public demo, which always uses Node's built-in `crypto.randomBytes`.

Live demo: https://tradepro-kumailr.vercel.app

TradePro is an algorithmic trading terminal — a real, working demo that charts live market data, scores trade setups, and runs paper trading, with trades and equity snapshots persisted to Supabase.

chunks.title: TradePro
chunks.text:
- **25-symbol watchlist** covering crypto and US equities, with a terminal-style interface in `public/`.
- **Real candlestick charts** built with TradingView's lightweight-charts library, with SMA overlays, a volume pane, and a live RSI subplot.
- **Technical analysis in Python**: the Flask backend in `api/` computes indicators (including SMA and RSI) and an 8-factor technical confluence gate that scores setups before a trade is suggested.
- **Manual order ticket** with risk-based position sizing using ATR-based stops.
- **SMA-crossover paper-trading engine** for backtesting-style simulated trades.
- **Market data from Yahoo Finance**, including daily closes for symbols such as AAPL, MSFT, TSLA, NVDA, and SPY.
- **Persistence in Supabase**: trades and equity snapshots are stored so a portfolio can be reviewed across sessions.

- Deployment: Vercel (`vercel.json`)
